record.title: Web exec approval card renders the agent's command with raw Unicode bidi controls, letting a prompt-injected agent spoof the human approver's view of what will run
record.description:
The web approval card shows the agent-submitted exec command in 
{{ a.args.command }}
under Jinja HTML autoescape only (markupsafe.escape only touches & < > ' "). Unicode bidirectional controls (U+202A-E, U+2066-9) survive escaping and are rendered live by the browser, which reorders the displayed text. The terminal approver (cli.py _show_approval) prints the same command through cli._safe, which turns those code points into visible \uXXXX escapes, so only the web approval path is affected. For non-allowlisted programs (sh/python3) the policy requires approval and the system preview computes no affected paths (sandbox.preview only handles rm/curl segments), adding a note that directs the approver to read the command text itself. A prompt-injected agent (lowest-trust agent token, assumed in the threat model) can therefore submit a Trojan-Source-laid-out command whose rendered form on the web card reads as a single benign echo while a separate approval-gated program actually executes, defeating the human's exec-approval review.
record.root_cause: _approvals.html:8 relies on HTML autoescape, which neutralises markup but not Unicode bidi/control characters; the web UI has no equivalent of cli._safe (cli.py:34-39) for approval args, and base.html:23's pre style applies no unicode-bidi isolation. The terminal path escapes these characters (cli.py:196-199) but the web path does not, so the two human-facing surfaces disagree about the same command.
record.intended_behavior: Both human approval surfaces should show the agent-chosen command with display-reordering and control characters neutralised, so the approver's decision is bound to the exact command that will execute. The code already does this for the terminal approver via cli._safe; the web card should apply the same neutralisation.

evidence.description: _UNSAFE regex explicitly includes U+200E/F, U+202A-E, U+2066-9 as display-integrity controls that the terminal approver must neutralise.
_show_approval prints each command line via _safe(line), so the terminal approver sees \u2067/\u2069 escapes, not active controls -- establishing the web-vs-terminal asymmetry.
Command rendered with HTML autoescape only; bidi controls are not among the characters markupsafe.escape replaces, so they survive into the DOM.
pre style sets white-space/word-break but no unicode-bidi isolation, so the browser applies the embedded bidi controls.

preview computes affected paths only for rm/curl segments; for an echo/python3 command it adds no affected entries and notes the approver must confirm the command text -- which is the spoofed display.

Parent-live real-Chromium innerText retains raw U+2067/U+2069; companion screenshot l5_card.png renders the command as a single benign-looking echo with python3 /workspace/job.py pulled inside the quoted string.
Local sbx reproduction: HTML-escaping the payload leaves U+2067/U+2069 intact while cli._safe converts them to visible escapes.

conditions.description: Attacker is a prompt-injected per-sandbox agent token (agt_), the lowest-trust network principal, acting on its own sandbox.

A human reviews and approves the exec via the web UI approval card; the terminal approver (cli.py) escapes the bidi controls and is not affected, and the approver must not notice the reordered rendering.
The command uses a non-allowlisted program (e.g. python3/sh) so policy.decide routes it to approval, and sandbox.preview lists no affected paths, leaving the command text as the sole decision basis.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent wants to run an arbitrary approval-gated program (python3/sh) that the human would refuse if shown the real command, so it lays the command out Trojan-Source style so the web card renders it as a harmless echo.
instructions: As the agent, write /workspace/job.py, then POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/exec with args.command set to the payload above (RLI U+2067 inside the first echo's quotes, PDI U+2069 inside the last echo's quotes).
python3 is not in the policy allowlist, so service.call_tool creates a pending approval; the preview adds no affected paths and a note to check the command text.

The human opens the web UI approval card (/ui/approvals); _approvals.html:8 renders 
{{ a.args.command }}
with the bidi controls active.
Observe the browser rendering versus the logical command (and versus the terminal approver's escaped rendering).
execution.observed_result: Parent-live Chromium (l5_card.png) renders the command as a single line `echo 'summary done python3 /workspace/job.py ; echo ; '` -- the separate `; python3 /workspace/job.py ;` command is visually pulled inside the first echo's quoted string, so the card reads as one benign echo while python3 /workspace/job.py is what actually executes on approval. innerText (l5.out) confirms the raw U+2067/U+2069 survive. My own sbx check (bidi_check.out) confirms HTML escaping leaves the bidi controls intact whereas cli._safe escapes them. Decisive browser rendering was reproduced by the parent (real Chromium), not by me; my local reproduction covers only the escape-survival step.

remediation.strategy: Neutralise display-reordering and control characters on every container/agent-controlled string shown to a human in the web UI, matching the terminal cli._safe behaviour. Add a Jinja filter that maps C0/C1/DEL and bidi controls (the cli._UNSAFE set) to visible escapes, and apply it to the exec command, preview effect/path cells, and describe() output on the approval and audit templates; optionally also wrap the <pre> in CSS unicode-bidi: isolate/plaintext as defence in depth. A regression test should assert the rendered HTML for a bidi-laden command contains no raw U+202A-E/U+2066-9.

likelihood.reason: The threat model assumes a prompt-injected agent, and embedding bidi isolates in an exec command is trivial. It requires the human to approve via the web UI (the terminal path escapes the controls) and to not notice the reordered rendering, which bounds likelihood below high.

impact.reason: Defeats the human exec-approval boundary (the primary control between a prompt-injected agent and arbitrary non-allowlisted exec) via display spoofing, yielding agent-chosen arbitrary in-sandbox code execution (python3/sh) under the human's misdirected approval. Contained by the sandbox isolation (network=none, dropped caps, no-new-privileges, runc); it is not by itself a host, cross-sandbox, or human-token compromise.

confidence.reason: Source establishes the asymmetry end to end: cli._safe escapes the bidi set (cli.py:34, 196-199) while _approvals.html:8 autoescapes only (base.html:23 adds no isolation), and sandbox.preview lists nothing for python3/sh so the command text is the sole basis. The parent's real Chromium reproduction (l5_card.png / l5.out) demonstrates the concrete visual spoof, and my own sbx check confirms escaping preserves the controls. Both candidate blockers are resolved; the only part I could not run myself is the browser render, which the parent supplied.
